open_points.subject: A30 CFG-001 required tests
open_points.text: The start-up check that the read bound is no larger than the response ceiling is a constraint of that table (`BINARY_MAX_READ_BYTES` less than or equal to `MAX_BINARY_RESPONSE_BYTES`), checked by `runtime_settings` at each `load_runtime_settings`, so a violating deployment does not start; `binary_storage` applies only the read bound, at each read.
open_points.question: Must the CFG-001 test demonstrate that the cross-bound constraint is rechecked on every invocation of `load_runtime_settings`, including invocations by the bootstrap command, `registry_gateway`, and `binary_storage`, or is demonstrating refusal during service start sufficient?
options: Test every listed `load_runtime_settings` call site and prove each rejects the invalid relation
Test only service start; later calls may assume the relation was already validated
open_points.default_guess: Test the loader directly on repeated calls and at least one non-startup caller, proving that every call rejects `BINARY_MAX_READ_BYTES > MAX_BINARY_RESPONSE_BYTES`.

witness.initial: All settings are individually well-typed, but `BINARY_MAX_READ_BYTES` is greater than `MAX_BINARY_RESPONSE_BYTES`.
events: The verification suite invokes `load_runtime_settings` only through service startup and observes refusal.
A later implementation invokes `load_runtime_settings` from another listed caller.
outcomes: An implementation that validates the relation only on the startup path passes the stated CFG-001 test.
An implementation that validates the relation on every loader call also passes the stated CFG-001 test.
witness.observer: A later agent implementing or verifying a non-startup caller sees whether the promised per-call constraint is actually enforced.

open_points.subject: runtime_settings failure at the bootstrap command
open_points.text: validated by `runtime_settings` at each call of `load_runtime_settings` (at start, by the bootstrap command, by `registry_gateway` at each Registry call and by the emitted `binary_storage` at each binary read)
open_points.question: When the new read-bound/response-ceiling constraint fails while the first-administrator bootstrap command calls `load_runtime_settings`, how is that refusal represented relative to the closed `BootstrapCommandOutcome` and `BOOTSTRAP_EXIT_CODES` catalogs?
options: Treat configuration rejection as an additional bootstrap outcome with a specified exit code
Fail before producing any `BootstrapCommandOutcome`, using a separately specified configuration-error exit behavior
Map the configuration rejection to one of the existing four bootstrap outcomes
open_points.default_guess: Fail before producing a bootstrap outcome and use a distinct, explicitly specified nonzero configuration-error exit behavior.

witness.initial: No staff account exists; every required environment value is present and individually valid, but `BINARY_MAX_READ_BYTES` exceeds `MAX_BINARY_RESPONSE_BYTES`.
events: The host operator runs the local first-administrator bootstrap command.
The command calls `load_runtime_settings`, which detects the new cross-bound violation before creating the account.
outcomes: The command terminates as a configuration failure outside the four closed bootstrap outcomes and uses an independently chosen exit code.
The command maps the failure into an existing bootstrap outcome or an implementer-added outcome and exit code.
witness.observer: The host operator and deployment automation observe different exit codes and failure classifications.
